To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) pre training a deep bidirectional transformer language model (BERT) and fine tuning it on downstream tasks is a simple yet powerful approach for achieving state of the art performance on a wide range of natural language processing tasks; (b) BERT is a robustly optimized Transformer and is effective on tasks involving a large quantity of unlabeled text such as question answering; (c) BERT is effective on tasks with limited amounts of labeled data, such as natural language inference and sentence classification; and
BERT is a deep bidirectional transformer based model pre trained with two unsupervised objectives, masked language modeling and next sentence prediction.

BERT is a new method for pre training deep bidirectional representations, that it achieves strong in domain performance on eleven natural language tasks, and that it is easy to fine tune to achieve state of the art performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) Can we learn deep bidirectional representations without labeled data? (2) Can these deep bidirectional representations be fine tuned with minimal task-specific architecture modifications for effective task generalization?
the following question: Can we pre train deep bidrectional representations of text from raw text alone? The answer, as demonstrated by our results, is yes.
the question: how to pre train a deep bidirectional language representation model that can be fine tuned to a wide variety of tasks?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model is able to achieve new state of the arts results in eleven natural language processing (NLP) tasks.
BERT is a new method for learning deep bidirectional representations for language.
BERT is a new language representation technique for pre training natural language processing systems, which is based on the bidirectional encoder representations from transformers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BERT is a robustly specified, robustly trained, and robustly evaluated model.
BERT, as a general purpose model, is a good off-the-shelf choice for the increasingly large NLP applications it can be directly applied to.
BERT is a general purpose language representation model that is pre trained on a large corpus of text data and used as an input embedding in a wide range of downstream tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bidirectional ELMo like contextual representations are a useful general purpose feature for a wide range NLP tasks.
deep bidirectional representations can be learned from plain text without access to any task specific supervision.

contextualized word representations learned by bidirectional Transformers can serve as a strong baseline for a wide range a natural language tasks, even when fine tuned with limited amounts of task specific training data.
